title: Judah, Son of Jacob
lead: Judah son of Jacob and Leah (the patriarch and his tribe; the later kingdom of Judah is a separate subject): he proposed selling Joseph, was confronted by Tamar, and later offered himself as a slave in Benjamin's place. Jacob gave him the scepter (Genesis 49:10). His tribe became the royal tribe of David, gave its name to the kingdom of Judah and to the Jews, and is the tribe of Jesus (Hebrews 7:14; Revelation 5:5).

sections.b: Judah's tribe leads Israel's march (Numbers 2:3; 10:14) and is the first to fight after Joshua (Judges 1:1–2). David, from Bethlehem in Judah, receives the kingship that Genesis 49:10 promised (1 Samuel 16; 2 Samuel 2:4; 5:3). Chronicles explains that "Judah grew strong among his brothers, and a ruler came from him," though the birthright went to Joseph (1 Chronicles 5:2), and the psalms celebrate God's choice: "He chose Judah's tribe instead" (Psalm 78:68); "Judah is my ruler's staff" (Psalm 60:7). After the kingdom split, the southern kingdom took Judah's name, and its people were called Yehudim, "Judahites," already before the exile (2 Kings 16:6; 25:25; Jeremiah 32:12). The same word later named the Jewish people wherever they lived, from Persia (Esther 2:5) to the returned community (Nehemiah 1:2), and gives English the word "Jew." The prophets look for a ruler from Judah (Micah 5:2), and the New Testament traces Jesus through Judah and Perez (Matthew 1:2–3; Luke 3:33) and calls him "the Lion from the tribe of Judah" (Revelation 5:5).
